title: Making the Most Out of Growing US-Uzbekistan Trade and Investment
author: Wilder Alejandro Sánchez
text:
Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev (center) with Sergio Gor (right), special envoy for South and Central Asia, and U.S. Senator Steve Daines (left), co-chair of the Senate Central Asia Caucus.
Credit: Uzbekistan Presidential Administration
The purchase of U.S.-made commercial aircraft and an Uzbek company’s historic opening of a manufacturing facility in Kentucky demonstrate the dynamic and growing economic relations between the United States and Uzbekistan. As U.S. diplomatic engagement with Tashkent increases – new contracts and trade and investment frameworks signed – understanding each country’s priorities and objectives will help explain this new chapter of the partnership. Moreover, stronger trade and investment numbers must translate into employment opportunities and an improved quality of life for the Uzbek population.Relations between Washington and Tashkent have generally strengthened over the past couple of years. U.S. President Donald Trump and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will next meet in December, as Trump has invited the Uzbek leader to be a guest at the G-20 summit in Miami.[...]
